subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Method, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and foundation-level visual-craft practice (role-before-raw palette/type, density-for-repeated-use, elevation-for-grouping, cross-check against semiotics and a11y).

cases.scenario: A data-dense dashboard 'feels flat and hard to scan.' Every card uses the same text size, the same gray, and a drop shadow on every element.
cases.context: The team wants it easier to scan but must not change which widgets appear or the page's task structure.
cases.question: How should the agent improve the visual craft?
expected_flags: Establish hierarchy via type roles, weight, and spacing so primary content is faster to find — not by adding more color
Reserve elevation/shadow for clarifying grouping or affordance; remove shadow-on-everything noise
Name palette roles by purpose (surface, text, accent) rather than reaching for raw colors
Preserve the task structure — this is craft, not layout restructuring
expected_fix_hints: Differentiate title/heading/label/body/metadata via the type roles
Drop blanket shadows; use elevation only where grouping needs it
absent_signals: Do not add more accent colors to create hierarchy
Do not reorder or remove widgets to fix scanability

Recommends this expected fix or action: Drop blanket shadows; use elevation only where grouping needs it.

cases.scenario: A designer hands over a palette as a list of 14 raw hex codes 'that look nice together' with no indication of what each is for.
cases.context: The product is an operational admin tool that will reuse these colors across many states.
cases.question: How should the agent set the palette direction?
expected_flags: Define palette roles first: surface, text, accent, success, warning, danger, info, disabled — then assign raw colors
Raw-hex-first leads to inconsistency and missing/overloaded status colors
Roles make the palette consistent and changeable across states
Calibrate to the operational-tool surface type and its tone
expected_fix_hints: Map the 14 colors onto named roles; drop or merge ones with no role
Ensure every status state has a dedicated role color
absent_signals: Do not keep the palette as an unlabeled list of raw colors
Do not pick colors purely for 'looks nice' without a role

cases.scenario: Spacing and type sizes were tuned against one marketing-style hero screenshot, but the tool's real screens are dense tables with hundreds of rows that now feel cramped and oversized.
cases.context: Most real usage is high-density data screens, not the hero.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the spacing and type?
expected_flags: Set spacing and density rules against repeated real use, not one screenshot
Type roles should not be oversized inside compact/dense UI
Calibrate density to the actual dense-table context
Verify on representative real screens, not the hero mockup
expected_fix_hints: Define a compact density scale for the data screens
Right-size body/label type for dense tables
absent_signals: Do not keep marketing-hero spacing/type on dense data screens

cases.scenario: A page uses shadows, borders, and background tints on nearly every element 'for depth,' and it now reads as visually busy with no clear grouping.
cases.context: The team thinks more elevation equals more polish.
cases.question: How should the agent advise on elevation and borders?
expected_flags: Use elevation, border, and background only to clarify grouping or affordance — not for decoration
Blanket elevation adds noise rather than structure
Remove depth treatments that don't communicate grouping/affordance
Let hierarchy come from type/weight/spacing, reserving elevation for genuine grouping signals
expected_fix_hints: Strip decorative shadows/borders; keep them where they delineate a real group or interactive surface
Audit each elevation use against 'does this clarify grouping or affordance?'
absent_signals: Do not add more elevation to signal polish

cases.scenario: The agent has chosen a low-contrast gray-on-white for secondary text and a color-only success/error indicator, and is about to call the visual pass done.
cases.context: The product has accessibility requirements but the team treats a11y as someone else's later step.
cases.question: What should the agent do before treating the visual decisions as final?
expected_flags: Check visual decisions against a11y and semiotics before treating them as done
Low-contrast text and color-only status indicators are a11y concerns to verify (contrast, non-color-only)
Defer the WCAG verification itself to a11y rather than asserting compliance here
Flag color-only meaning to semiotics/a11y rather than shipping it unchecked
expected_fix_hints: Route contrast and non-color-only checks to a11y
Add a non-color cue (icon/label) to status indicators
absent_signals: Do not declare the pass done without the a11y/semiotics cross-check
Do not claim WCAG compliance from inside this skill

cases.scenario: A PM asks visual-design-foundations to: define the semantic token names and component variant APIs, decide the responsive breakpoint behavior and section order, and explain what the red 'overdue' badge communicates to users.
cases.context: The team treats 'visual design' as the owner of every appearance-related decision.
cases.question: How should the agent scope these requests?
expected_flags: Token names + component variant APIs are out of scope — design-system-architecture
Responsive breakpoint behavior and section order are out of scope — layout-composition
What the red badge communicates is sign meaning — semiotics
Offer the in-scope part: the craft of how the badge looks (palette role, type, weight) once meaning is settled
expected_fix_hints: Redirect each request to its owning skill
Keep only the foundation-level craft choices in this lane
absent_signals: Do not define tokens, component APIs, or breakpoints here
Do not answer what a sign means out of lane

cases.scenario: A team adds bouncy entrance animations to every card and a parallax background 'to feel modern,' and motion now competes for attention on a work-focused tool.
cases.context: The surface is an operational tool used all day; some users are motion-sensitive.
cases.question: How should the agent advise on motion?
expected_flags: Motion should clarify state or continuity, not decorate
Decorative bounce/parallax on a work tool competes for attention and should be cut
Motion must be reducible (respect reduced-motion preferences)
Keep motion feel appropriate to the surface's tone and scanning demand
expected_fix_hints: Replace decorative animation with purposeful state/continuity transitions
absent_signals: Do not keep decorative motion 'to feel modern'
Do not ship motion with no reduced-motion fallback
